No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. ## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e82725a185db27b45fcb83bc775d682855582db8`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/hook-run-as.ts, packages/objectql/src/hook-wrappers.ts, packages/objectql/src/hook-run-as.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/runas-user-hook-org-peers.integration.test.ts, .changeset/24497-hook-runas-org-peers.md + packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts (`resolveAuthzContext`, `vetOrganizationClaim`, `resolveUserAuthzGrants`, `ResolveUserAuthzGrantsOptions`), packages/core/src/security/resolve-user-grants-cache.ts (`openUserGrantsCache`), packages/core/src/security/request-grants-memo.ts (`openRequestGrantsMemo`), packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts (`resolveRunContext`, `FlowUserGrants`), packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin.ts (the grants bridge), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts (`resolvePermissionSetsForContextUnmemoized`), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/objects/default-permission-sets.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts (`SYSTEM_CTX`, `mirrorStatusField`, `redeemActionToken`), packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-node.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/lifecycle-hooks.ts, packages/runtime/src/stored-metadata-reader-seam.ts (`deriveThroughSeam`), packages/runtime/src/sandbox/body-runner.ts (`buildSandboxApi`), packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/execution-context.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/scoped-context.ts (`IScopedContext`), packages/objectql/src/index.ts, packages/objectql/package.json, packages/core/src/security/second-object-read-exposure.pin.test.ts, scripts/check-system-context-census.mjs, .github/workflows/lint.yml, .github/workflows/pr-automation.yml (WHICH LEVEL), content/docs/automation/hooks.mdx, content/docs/automation/hook-bodies.mdx, content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx. Base: merge-base `3ae0b777d4b94187abedc74f3ae316ff8e063e35`; the diff is 6 files, +441/-10, matching the PR's file list. Card #24497 with every comment (triage 6263439195, claim 6263990919, dispatch 6264023108, report 6265315507, all read as claims), #24448 and PR #24495 with its review 6263414965 and rework record 6262868933, ruling A′ 6261536443 item 2, #24341's blocker note 6263655119, PR #24518's body, and the head's check-runs.

### ① Derived judgments

**What a `runAs: 'user'` hook may read, before and after.** The seed is `ScopedContext.withUserGrantsSeeded` (engine.ts), awaited by `installRunAsApi` (hook-wrappers.ts) through `seedHookUserGrants` (hook-run-as.ts) for `'user'` only. Its two predicates are `needsGrants = !Array.isArray(ctx.permissions)` and `needsPeers = !Array.isArray(ctx.org_user_ids)`; it returns `this` when neither holds, otherwise makes ONE `resolveUserAuthzGrants(this.engine, ctx.userId, tenantId ? { tenantId } : {})` call and spreads the answer onto a copy of the pin. Per triggering shape:

- *Request-resolved (control):* `resolveAuthzContext` copies `positions`, `permissions` and `org_user_ids` as arrays onto every request context (resolve-authz-context.ts `ctx.org_user_ids = grants.org_user_ids`, with the anonymous `[]` seed). Both predicates are false, zero reads, same envelope. Before equals after. Pinned at both layers (unit: `reads(engine)` empty; real stack: envelope verbatim). Right.
- *`{ isSystem: true, userId, tenantId }` (the card's shape):* before, `withRunAs('user')` pinned `{ ...ctx, isSystem: false }` with no sets and no list; the security plugin applied its additive member baseline to the user-id'd context (`resolvePermissionSetsForContextUnmemoized`: `positions ?? []`, `permissions ?? []`, `member_default` added for a caller with a `userId`) and `sys_user_org_members` compiled `unresolved-variable` and dropped out, so the hook saw its own row. After, both predicates hold: positions, permission sets and the peer list (the members of `tenantId` plus the user, resolver step 5) are seeded; the baseline is still added on top, exactly as on the request. Measured `[usr_me]` to `[usr_me, usr_peer]`, `usr_other` and `usr_loner` never present. Right.
- *Approvals' `SYSTEM_CTX` `{ isSystem: true, positions: [], permissions: [], userId }`:* `Array.isArray([])` is true, so `needsGrants` is false and the empty arrays stay verbatim; `needsPeers` holds and the resolver, asked with no tenant, answers `org_user_ids: [userId]` (its seed value; step 5 runs only under a tenant). Before: no list. After: `[usr_me]`, sets `[]`. The empty-array treatment is the same as `resolveRunContext`'s `!Array.isArray(runContext.permissions)` (service-automation engine.ts), so "carried positions and permission sets stay verbatim, only the peer list is taken" holds for empty arrays too. Pinned on the real stack (case 4). Right.
- *A narrowed agent ceiling:* carries non-empty `permissions`, so it stays verbatim; only the peer list is added. Right. One shape neither twin guards: a context carrying `positions` but no `permissions` has its positions REPLACED (the predicate keys on `permissions` alone). No shipped producer hands that shape (the doors forward both or neither), and the replacement is the user's own resolved positions, so it is not a widening past the request. Noted, not blocking.
- *No organisation `{ isSystem: true, userId }`:* resolver with no tenant: `org_user_ids: [userId]`, positions and sets from the global rows only (`grantAppliesInTenant`). Identical to an organisation-less request. Pinned at both layers. Right.
- *No `userId`:* `withRunAs('user')` returns `UnscopedHookApi`; `seedHookUserGrants` hands it through (no `withUserGrantsSeeded` member); the data door still refuses `HOOK_UNSCOPED_DATA_ACCESS`; `engine.seen` is empty. Pinned. Right.
- *A context that already carries a list* resolves nothing: `needsPeers` false; with sets present, `return this`. Pinned (zero `find` calls). Right.

**Open question 1, the widening from the baseline to the user's real grants.** It is exactly what the same user's request holds, and never more. `resolveAuthzContext` copies `grants.positions` and `grants.permissions` from the same resolver call onto a request; the security plugin adds the same baseline additively to both envelopes. The hook's pin is the request's envelope MINUS `systemPermissions`, `accessible_org_ids` and `posture` (not seeded, as on the flow side), so it is a subset. It cannot exceed the triggering context's ceiling anywhere: a trigger that carries a ceiling (non-empty `permissions`) keeps it verbatim, and a trigger with none was `isSystem: true`, which has no ceiling to exceed. Option A is right: one resolver, one rule for both producers, which is what ruling A′ item 2 asks.

**The tenant the seed resolves under** is the triggering context's `tenantId`, as handed, unvetted. The request path vets a claimed organisation against `grants.accessible_org_ids` under a walled posture (`vetOrganizationClaim`) and drops an unbacked claim before re-resolving; the hook has no posture to ask. So a producer that hands `{ userId: U, tenantId: T }` with U not a member of T would give the hook T's members, which is more than U's own request under `isolated` or `group`. The list is always ONE organisation, never a union (step 5 reads `sys_member` for `tenantId` only; pinned by `usr_other`'s absence). No shipped producer hands an unbacked tenant: `approval-node.ts` passes the flow context's own `tenantId`, `mirrorStatusField` and `redeemActionToken` pass none. This is the inference PR #24495's review accepted for flows ("the run takes the trigger's tenantId as handed"); accepted here with the condition named. `grants.accessible_org_ids` is in the same resolver answer if a later card wants the hook to vet.

**Failure mode.** The rejection arm of `installRunAsApi` installs `derived`, the unseeded `{ ...ctx, isSystem: false }` pin, and warns once; nothing from a partial resolution is applied, because the resolver throws `AuthzStoreUnavailableError` before it returns. Policies reading `org_user_ids` drop out and the sets are unchanged (baseline where none). Nothing is widened relative to before the PR: fail-closed for access. The request path answers a store failure with 503 where the hook runs degraded with a warning; that divergence is the flow twin's accepted posture (`resolveRunContext`'s catch). Pinned (`org_user_ids` undefined, one warn naming `current_user.org_user_ids drops out`). Right.

**`'inherit'`, `'system'`, the refusal.** `runAs === 'inherit' ? noRestore : await installRunAsApi(...)` keeps `'inherit'` free of any await and the api the same reference (pinned). `'system'` still installs `sudo()`; its restore now comes back through `Promise.resolve`, one tick, no resolver read (pinned `reads(sys)` empty). The `UnscopedHookApi` refusal does not move. Right.

**`withRunAs` stays synchronous.** Two reasons, both real. `RunAsDerivableApi.withRunAs` is a synchronous member of a type exported from objectql's index, so an async return would be a contract change on a published type. And runtime's `deriveThroughSeam` wraps `withRunAs`'s return value synchronously in its derivation walk; a Promise there would be wrapped as a Promise and the awaited context would be unserved. The ordering the PR relies on holds: the body runner's `buildSandboxApiSource` reads `engineCtx.api` at handler time, inside the wrapped hook after `installRunAsApi` has swapped in the seeded api, and `buildSandboxApi` wraps it then; the in-process hook api is not seam-served at all. Right. The consequence for the new member is in ②.

**The grants cache, open question 3.** `openUserGrantsCache` returns `undefined` when `OS_AUTHZ_GRANTS_CACHE_TTL_MS` is `0`, the shipped default, so the seed resolves byte-identically to the uncached path. The bypass list is a ruled list of two sites with two reasons (the explainer verifying a revocation; long-lived automation runs that must not pin an envelope). A hook pins its api for one handler call and the cache retires entries on writes to the objects the resolver reads; neither reason applies. No bypass is right, and adding a third site to a ruled list without a ruling would itself be a deviation. The request memo is inert here (no `resolveAuthzContext` scope), as the PR body says.

**The census.** The first version read `ctx.isSystem` inside `withUserGrantsSeeded` and `check-system-context-census` refused it `[site-without-a-row]`; `e82725a1` removed the read instead of anchoring a row. Right: the method runs only on the api `withRunAs('user')` built, whose `isSystem` is `false` by construction, so the read was a branch that could not fire, and a row would have documented a behaviour that does not exist. The census gate runs in `Lint · repo & tooling gates` (lint.yml) and is success on this head. Core's `[#22661]` census enumerates reads resolved through `referenceTargetOf` (second-object-read-exposure.pin.test.ts); callers of `resolveUserAuthzGrants` are not its population, and no pin counts those callers (nine non-test callers at the base). No row owed. Right.

**#24341's precondition.** On a `runAs: 'user'` hook's pin `org_user_ids` is now always an array (at least `[userId]`), except after a resolver failure. So under the one-policy default `id == current_user.id || id in current_user.org_user_ids`, a hook fired from approvals' envelopes keeps its own `sys_user` row (pinned on the real stack: `org_user_ids: ['usr_me']` from the exact `SYSTEM_CTX` plus `userId`). Peers from `mirrorStatusField` need the producer to carry an organisation, which it deliberately does not; `approval-node.ts` already carries the flow's `tenantId`, so that producer's hook sees peers after this PR. Met, with the resolver-failure edge (no list, so the self arm drops too) that PR #24495's review accepted and told #24341's seat.

**One derivation outside the seam's walk.** `deriveThroughSeam` lists what a scoped API can derive (`object`, `sudo`, `withRunAs`, `transaction`, `beginTransaction`) so that "neither layer can leave a route around it". `withUserGrantsSeeded` is a new public derivation that walk does not know: a seam-served host action handler's `ctx.api` (action-execution.ts) calling it receives an unserved `ScopedContext`. Not an access widening (host code is deployer trust and reaches the store through its own imports; the body layers are the boundary and a body's api carries `object` and `transaction` only), but the published invariant gains an exception. Closed by keeping the member off the public face, see ②.

### ② Semver level

`ScopedContext` is exported from `packages/objectql/src/index.ts`, `ObjectQL.createContext()` returns it, `@objectstack/objectql` publishes with `access: public`, and nothing strips internal members from the built declarations. The new public async method is therefore a member of the published surface, reachable from an exported factory's return. Under the Check Changeset step's WHICH LEVEL rule (maintainer ruling 2026-09-04 on #15294) as PR #24495's patch round read it (rework record 6262868933, review 6263414965: an optional member added to an exported type is an additive widening, `minor`), a new public method on an exported class is at least that. As committed, `'@objectstack/objectql': patch` with `Clause-②: no` is the same misdeclaration #24495 corrected in its patch round. `Check Changeset` is success because `patch` and `no` are a consistent pair; it does not judge whether `no` is true.

The method can be kept off the public face, and that is the reviewer's call, because it also closes the seam-walk gap in ①: key the member on a symbol declared in `hook-run-as.ts` and not re-exported from `index.ts` (the wrapper already reaches it by duck-typing through `seedHookUserGrants`, and `engine.ts` already imports from `./hook-run-as.js`, so no new import cycle), or any equivalent that leaves no nameable member on `ScopedContext`'s declarations. Then the changeset stays `'@objectstack/objectql': patch` and the `Clause-②: no (...)` line stands as written in the changeset and on the PR body.

If the seat instead keeps the public method, the PR body's second line and the changeset's last line must both read `Clause-②: yes (widening: ScopedContext, exported from objectql's index, gains the public async method withUserGrantsSeeded(); no accepted input moves)` and the changeset's level must read `'@objectstack/objectql': minor`; the seam's derivation walk then owes the member as well, which is a runtime edit outside this card's fence.

Either way the head as committed does not hold on ②. The access face is accepted as it stands.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`engine.ts` import line** (`resolveUserAuthzGrants` added to the existing `@objectstack/core` import): in substance inside the fence, since it serves the `ScopedContext` member the claim named; not PR #24508's predicate region, which has since landed on `main` with no conflict against this branch. Accepted.
- **The probe in `service-automation`** (`domain:services`): a test file only, beside its flow twin, in the one package whose devDependencies compose the stack; no dependency or lockfile change. Accepted as a cross-lane test rider; the `domain:services` seat is told at landing.
- **No real approvals write path**: the probe fires the exact envelopes I read (`SYSTEM_CTX` in `approval-service.ts` and `approval-node.ts`, plus `userId`). Accepted; the gap is stated in the PR.
- **Full objectql suite not run locally**: `Test Core` 1/6 to 6/6 are success on this head. Accepted.
- **Trailers**: the commits carry the model-free pair AGENTS.md prescribes; the harness-written trailer is AGENTS.md's exemption, not its rule. Not a deviation.
- **Open questions**: 1 answered A (①). 2 answered in ②: the declaration as committed is wrong; the route is named. 3 answered A (①).
- **Out-of-scope finding 1** (approvals' envelopes carry no `tenantId`): half right. `mirrorStatusField` carries `userId` only, by documented design (`tenantId` is a driver-scoping knob on that write and would no-op the mirror cross-org). `approval-node.ts` DOES carry `tenantId: context?.tenantId` beside the non-envelope `organizationId`, so the finding's account of that producer is wrong; its hook sees peers whenever the flow context carries a tenant. The `mirrorStatusField` half meets filing gate ①, class (a): a named producer whose user context names no organisation, measured (own row where the user's request sees peers). Lane `domain:services`. The card is a decision on how an attribution-only write names the organisation it acts in, not "add `tenantId`". File, corrected.
- **Out-of-scope finding 2** (`SYSTEM_CTX`'s empty arrays keep a hook on the baseline): right. Meets gate ①, class (a), `domain:services`, as the hook-side #3356 gap for this producer; omitting the empty arrays when naming a user lets this PR's seed resolve. The direction worth stating on the card: for a user whose grants sit below the baseline (`viewer_readonly` is resolved instead of the member baseline), the baseline is WIDER than the user's request. That is the pre-existing shape, unchanged by this PR. File.
- **Out-of-scope finding 3** (`systemPermissions`, `accessible_org_ids`, posture not carried): `carrier: none`, the same note PR #24495 carried. No measured consequence; the `group` wall reading `accessible_org_ids` is what to measure first. Stays in the PR's notes, not filed.
- **Docs**: `content/docs/automation/hooks.mdx` publishes `'user'` as "the triggering user, so the hook can never exceed that user's grants", which stays true. The three drift-flagged pages name `ScopedContext` only. No docs edit owed.
- **Check-runs on `e82725a1`** (read 2026-10-19T11:10Z): 40, all completed; 34 success, 6 skipped (Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, the Dogfood shard matrix, Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke, Temporal Conformance), 0 failed. `Test Core` 2/6 and 4/6 were in progress at my first read (11:01Z) and completed success. `Lint & Repo Gates`, every `Type Check ·` job, `Build Core`, `Check Changeset` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` are success.
- **Landing**: not now. One patch round: take `withUserGrantsSeeded` off the public face (or declare the widening and raise the level, with the seam walk owed), then a new record on the new head. #24341's seat is told that the precondition is met for approvals' envelopes, with the resolver-failure edge.
